lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Decided in Threes
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Juliane Albieri Calixto | Lesson 7 -- Decided in Threes
lesson.grammar_point: passive voice in the present and in the past: is / are made, was / were approved, by + who

listenings.text: Hi, it's Oliver again. Let me tell you about an idea I loved. I wanted a short video to explain every fee in our app. The idea was presented to the trio, and at first everybody liked it. But then the tech lead pushed back. Every fee changes twice a year, so every video would need to be made again. It wasn't feasible. So the idea was cut from the scope. I was sad for one day. Then a simpler solution was designed: short texts with a small icon, written with the legal team. They were tested with users, and they worked better than my videos. Lesson learned: the best idea is the one that is built.

Hi, Priya here. People often ask me how our roadmap is made. It's reviewed every three months. First, ideas are collected from everybody: designers, engineers, sales, and of course users. Then every idea is compared with two things: the goals of the company and the data from users. The final list is decided in the trio, by consensus. Not every idea is chosen, and that's normal. The ideas that are not chosen are kept in a list, and some of them come back later. My favorite feature this year was rejected twice before it was approved. So my advice to designers is simple: don't give up on a good idea.
